 FDA Recall Update: October 2026 
 Undeclared ingredients was the reason for many recalls during the month. There were 26 recalls in the food & beverage sector, a notable increase over September.
 Nicole Schlosser , Managing Editor , Powder & Bulk Solids November 5, 2026
 4 Min Read Hummus was one of a handful of food products recalled for undeclared sesame. Getty Images/iStockphoto The US Food & Drug Administration (FDA) recalled 26 food & beverage products, including 3 dietary supplements and 1 pet food product during the month of October. 
 Similar to last month, the biggest reasons for recalls made during October were potential for foodborne illness-causing bacteria: Listeria monocytogenes (4) , Salmonella (3) , E. coli (3) , and in one case, potential Clostridium botulinum . 
 Still, several recalls were also issued due to undeclared allergens (milk, nuts, sesame, and soy). 
 Other food and beverage recalls were issued for potential foreign material contamination (glass, metal, pests), and yeast and mold. 
 Foodborne Concerns Persist 
 As with September, last month saw recalls for frozen blueberries and mixed berries due to potential E. coli contamination and for broccoli sprouts and seeds due to possible Salmonella contamination. 
 On October 15, the FDA added broccoli seeds to a Salmonella outbreak linked to sprouts that sickened more than 30 people across six states. The agency’s investigation into the outbreak was initially linked to broccoli sprouts and microgreens as of September. That outbreak, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention announced on November 4, is now over, and the FDA’s investigation is complete . 
 Related: USDA Recall Update for October 2026 
 Additionally, recalls for frozen blueberries and mixed berries have persisted over the last few months and into October. A recall was initially issued in July by Chile-based frozen berries producer Frutas y Hortalizas del Sur S.A. for 10-oz bags of GreenWise Organic IQF Organic Blueberries. That grew and was updated to a Class I recall , representing the highest level of risk, in August. In October, the recall also impacted brands sold at Walmart and Trader Joe’s. 
 Dietary, Pet Medicine Recalls 
 Three dietary supplements were recalled due to containing prescription medicine ingredients Sildenafil, Tadalafil, and Dapoxetine (1), undeclared alcohol compounds (1), and presence of a drug no longer approved for medical use (1). 
 The pet food recall was issued for veterinary medications, because of potential potency issues. 
 Recalls Inch Back Up 
 The number of FDA recalls for food and beverages made in October is more than 20% higher than September, which saw a sharp drop in the number of recalls compared to the previous month. August had the second-highest number of recalls in 2026 so far, and May had the most , at 38. July’s total of 13 recalls in the food and beverage sector was another low that aligned more closely with recalls in 2 spring months — April, with 13 recalls , and February, with 14 recalls .

 About the Author
 Nicole Schlosser
 Managing Editor, Powder & Bulk Solids 
 Nicole Schlosser is the managing editor at Powder & Bulk Solids . She has worked as a writer and editor for nearly two decades, including for several B2B publications. Nicole has covered various aspects of the public and private transportation industries, including vehicle manufacturing, fueling, safety, and fleet management. She has also written about the specialty chemicals and materials, biotech, metals and mining, fintech, portfolio management, and leisure industries. Her work has appeared in The Wall Street Transcript , LP Gas magazine , School Bus Fleet , and Metro magazine , among others. Nicole earned her MFA in Creative Writing, with an emphasis on Playwrighting, from St. Mary's College of California, and her B.A. in Theater from Illinois State University.
